items.title: Lew Tabackin interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: When I played with Duke Pearson’s band, the saxes were me and Frank Foster were the tenor players

ctx.x: I see that all the time. They put the weakest player on the fourth tenor and then they ruin the sax section like that. When I played with Duke Pearson’s band, the saxes were me and Frank Foster were the tenor players, and he played the bottom tenor, which was right. Because at that time my sound — my sound changed through the years — at that point it was kind of, I was still in a little kind of Coltrane — the sound was kind of bright, and it was kind of the end of a period for me. And Frank had this lovely, big…
Now did you guys decide that? Or did Duke Pearson recognize it.
